title: Definability: parameters, symmetries, and what formulas can describe
summary: Describe subsets and function graphs by formulas, test definitions using symmetries, and count the limits of finite parameters.
abstract: Strict order tells us which real number lies to the right of another, but it does not single out where the positive numbers begin. Supplying zero as a parameter makes that ray easy to describe. Definability asks which subsets, relations, and function graphs can be described by a formula with specified parameters. Combining formulas and asking for witnesses produces more definable sets. Every such definition must respect the symmetries that leave its parameters fixed, which gives a way to prove that some descriptions are impossible. Symmetry alone does not settle the question: even a structure with no nontrivial symmetries has undefinable subsets when its domain is infinite and its language is countable.
